payload.stem: DNA standards of known size and an unknown fragment were separated by gel electrophoresis. The table shows how far each band migrated. On a graph of the logarithm of fragment size against distance migrated, the points of neighboring standards fall on a straight line. Which of the following is the best estimate of the size of the unknown fragment?

stimulus.description: Distance migrated by DNA standards and by an unknown fragment in an agarose gel

options.why: Uses the size of the nearest standard band.

The unknown band lies between the 5,000 bp and 3,000 bp standards. It is 0.67 of the way between them. On the log scale, log10(size) = log10(5000) + 0.67(log10(3000) - log10(5000)), which gives a size of about 3,550 bp.
Uses the larger of the two bracketing standards.
Uses the midpoint of the two bracketing sizes.

items.stem: The population size stops changing at the end of the table. Which value is the best estimate of the carrying capacity of the island for this population?

options.why: Reads the starting population size.
The last three counts (792, 798, and 800) are nearly the same, so the population has leveled off at about 800, which is the carrying capacity.
Reads the population size in year 4, which is still increasing.
Reads the population size in the year of fastest growth.

items.explanation_en:
The correct answer is 800. The last three counts (792, 798, and 800) are nearly the same, so the population has leveled off at about 800, which is the carrying capacity.
10 is incorrect: Reads the starting population size.
162 is incorrect: Reads the population size in year 4, which is still increasing.
426 is incorrect: Reads the population size in the year of fastest growth.

items.stem: A drought reduces the amount of plant food available on the island. Which prediction about the mouse population is best supported?

options.text: The carrying capacity would increase, because competition for the remaining food would be stronger.
options.why: A loss of resources lowers, not raises, the carrying capacity.

options.text: The population would increase without limit, because fewer plants mean fewer competitors.
options.why: A reduction of the food supply does not remove limits on a population.

options.text: The carrying capacity would decrease, and the population would decline toward a smaller size.
options.why: Fewer resources can support fewer individuals, so the population falls toward the lower carrying capacity.

options.text: The carrying capacity would stay the same, and the population would continue to grow at the same rate.
options.why: The carrying capacity is set by the resources, which have decreased.

items.explanation_en:
The correct answer is The carrying capacity would decrease, and the population would decline toward a smaller size.. Fewer resources can support fewer individuals, so the population falls toward the lower carrying capacity.
The carrying capacity would increase, because competition for the remaining food would be stronger. is incorrect: A loss of resources lowers, not raises, the carrying capacity.
The population would increase without limit, because fewer plants mean fewer competitors. is incorrect: A reduction of the food supply does not remove limits on a population.
The carrying capacity would stay the same, and the population would continue to grow at the same rate. is incorrect: The carrying capacity is set by the resources, which have decreased.

One governing relationship, no calculation, light reading; fits a typical full-mock item.
